newsitem.title: REUNION: Civil servants end 12-day strike on Reunion.
newsitem.headline: Civil servants end 12-day strike on Reunion.

text.p: Civil servants protesting at French plans to cut their pay staged a final rally on Monday to end a 12-day strike on the Indian Ocean island of Reunion.
An estimated 2,500 people took part in the rally. Civil servants and students also ended an occupation of a local government office in the centre of Saint-Denis.
Unions agreed at the weekend to suspend the stoppages to pave the way to talks with a government-appointed mediator, Pierre Lagourgue, from Tuesday.
The protests have included huge marches, that have sometimes triggered looting and violent clashes with riot police.
The workers started the strike on March 6, mainly over government plans to start phasing out the extra 53 percent in salaries paid to civil servants stationed in France's overseas possessions.

Reunion, with a population of about 600,000 Creoles, Indians, Chinese and Europeans, is a divided society. Some benefit from the high salaries and have European standards of living, the rest try to scrape a living from the depressed sugar cane business.
